Connor to run baseline latency/cost benchmark on Aurora staging (results by 2027-09-12)

summary: Quick technical alignment on joint marketplace listing and reference architecture. Reviewed integration points for private deployments (VPC peering, KMS), discussed benchmarks and next steps for a 2-week POC. Agreed to share a draft reference arch and run initial latency/cost tests.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call - I m Maya from Redwood, Connor and Zara here from our eng team. Evan, Priya, Marco, you there?
[00:12] Evan Brooks: Yep, here. Thanks Maya. Evan from AuroraCloud.
[00:16] Priya Narayanan: Priya, hi.
[00:18] Marco Ruiz: Marco here.
[00:20] Maya Patel: Great, thanks. The goal today is to sync on the joint solution for the Aurora marketplace listing and the reference architecture for private deployments. We want to align on network, security, and the initial benchmark plan.
[00:34] Connor Li: I ll jump in on the technical bits — we re expecting two main integration patterns: 1) marketplace listing where customers can subscribe to Redwood hosted inference via Aurora marketplace and 2) a private integration where Aurora customers can deploy Redwood in their VPC or we do a private partner-managed offering.
[00:50] Priya Narayanan: Quick clarifying question — for the private mode, are you suggesting Redwood runs in our customers' VPC or Aurora hosts a managed appliance?
[01:00] Maya Patel: Good q. We support both. For the partner joint solution we typically document two reference archs: a hosted-first flow (Redwood Dedicated behind Aurora marketplace entitlements) and a VPC-peered private flow where Redwood Private is deployed into customer VPC or a partner-managed enclave.
[01:18] Evan Brooks: Okay that s helpful. From Aurora ops perspective we need details about egress rules, ports, and KMS integration for key rotation. Also around audit logs — our compliance team will want to see retention windows.
[01:32] Connor Li: Right. For KMS we support BYOK via standard customer KMS or partner KMS integrations. There might be a small note in the doc where kernel selection, oh sorry, kernel selection — I mean runtime kernels — might behave differently under heavy quantized models. So we ll call out recommended instance types and quantization profiles.
[01:55] Marco Ruiz: On the marketplace listing itself, what are the marketing / metadata requirements? Like screenshots, billing SKU config, trial entitlements, etc.
[02:04] Maya Patel: We have a template. I ll share the marketplace listing template — it covers SKU mapping, trial credits, support levels, and required legal/SLAs. We ll also include example pricing tiers tied to token rates and dedicated capacity.
[02:20] Evan Brooks: It would help if you can supply example benchmark numbers — p99 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens for the recommended config. Our customers will compare that to CloudX and NovaEdge.
[02:33] Connor Li: Yes — we can run a baseline on a gpt-like open model and share results. Prospective caveat: latency depends heavily on sequence length and batching. We ll include a matrix of expected throughput at different batch sizes.
[02:48] Priya Narayanan: About security stuff — SAML SSO for marketplace control plane, SCIM for provisioning, SOC2/ISO artifacts. Can you share the SOC2 report?
[02:58] Maya Patel: We ll share a SOC2 summary and the security checklist. Note some names may be in the security pdf that the transcription might garble — but we ll get the artifacts over.
[03:09] Marco Ruiz: Any blockers on the POC side? We re thinking of a 2-week POC where we test a sample customer workflow: private deployment with KV cache, LLM endpoint, and cost tracking.
[03:20] Connor Li: That s doable. For the private POC we ll need access — temporary IAM role or a peered VPC with a small subnet. Also we ll need to know if you ll allow egress to public container registries or if we need to provide an airgapped image.
[03:36] Evan Brooks: We can do peered VPC. For customers in regulated sectors they want air-gapped images; most customers are fine with peering for the initial POC.
[03:45] Priya Narayanan: On observability, can Redwood produce per-route latency/cost traces and token-level breakdowns? We want to show customers the cost savings when we enable KV cache and batching.
[03:57] Zara Kim: Yep, Redwood Console exposes per-route token counts, cost breakdown, and tracing hooks. There s also a rollouts page where you can do canary and fallback to lighter models. Note the console name is Redwood Console but it sometimes gets transcribed as "Redwood Consolee" in automated notes.
[04:14] Maya Patel: Also we'll provide a short demo screencap of the console to include in the marketplace listing.
[04:20] Marco Ruiz: About billing — how does usage metering map to Aurora marketplace SKUs? We d prefer a usage-to-SKU bridge that bills via marketplace but reports into Redwood usage logging.
[04:31] Maya Patel: We ve implemented metering hooks before; typical approach is metered usage pushed to marketplace connector and a billing reconciliation file. We ll provide the spec for the connector mapping.
[04:43] Evan Brooks: Great. On legal/compliance we ll need to confirm data residency for EU customers — is there a region pinning option?
[04:51] Connor Li: Yes, customers can pin to specific regions for Dedicated/Private deployments. We ll include the region mapping table in the ref arch doc.
[04:59] Priya Narayanan: Any mention of model versioning and rollouts — we want deterministic rollbacks in case of regressions.
[05:06] Zara Kim: We support version pinning and canary rollouts with automatic fallback polcies — sometimes transcribed as "fallback policies" or "fond back" but it s fallback. We also integrate with eval harnesses to monitor quality regressions against provided prompt sets.
[05:22] Marco Ruiz: Sounds good. Let s talk timeline — if you share the ref arch and security artifacts by Tuesday (that s 2027-09-07) we can spin up the staging network and aim to start the POC week of 2027-09-20.
[05:34] Maya Patel: That s aligned with our plan. I ve captured action items: I ll send the reference arch and marketplace template; Connor will run the baseline; Evan will provide network info.
[05:45] Evan Brooks: One last note — some customers ask about on-prem option for airgapped deployments. Do you have an on-prem bundle or is that a custom engagement?
[05:55] Connor Li: We have a Redwood Private on-prem package but it s often a custom engagement for heavy-regulated customers. We ll include a reference note in the doc.
[06:04] Priya Narayanan: Okay thanks, this was helpful.
[06:08] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone, we ll follow up with the artifacts and ping to schedule the POC kickoff.
[06:14] Marco Ruiz: Thanks, bye.
[06:16] (recording stops)
